title: Deus Ex 总监 Warren Spector 宣布退休，结束近 45 年游戏生涯
content:
Deus Ex director Warren Spector is retiring after almost 45 years
Business
News
Deus Ex director Warren Spector is retiring after nearly 45 years in game dev
Spector 'thinks' he's retiring for good, despite having ideas for three games he'd love to make.
Diego Argüello
,
Contributing Editor, News
,
GameDeveloper.com
August 18, 2026
3 Min Read
Image via OtherSide Entertainment
Warren Spector, the veteran game developer who worked on the likes of
System Shock
,
Deus Ex
and most recently
Thick as Thieves
, is retiring after 43 years.
Spector shared the news earlier today
via LinkedIn
, where his profile now shows "retired" as his current job. "I'm retiring from game development," he writes. "At least I think so. I've been here before and changed my mind but this time I'm pretty sure I mean it."
The developer goes on to remember his career a month away from his 44th year in the industry. In that time he shipped 17 full games, and around "nine or so" add-on packs.
"I've run teams as small as a dozen and as big as 800," Spector says. "I've worked for big companies and done startups. I like to think I've helped some insanely talented people along in their careers. (That last is the most important.)"
Now, the developer says that with age and health catching up to him, he's feeling like he's done what he was set out to do. For the time being, he's set on writing and reading books, do lecturing, and potentially do consulting.
Related:
Harvey Smith and fellow Arkane Austin veterans announce a new studio, Black Pony Immersive
Yet, Spector admits having "mixed feelings" about the decision, especially since there are three games in particular he'd still like to make: one that's very big, one that's very small, and one he doesn't know how to make.
"But the game business has changed and it's just not as much fun for me anymore," he says. "Plus there's a new generation of developers coming up who deserve their time in the sun."
Spector's latest venture yielded uneven results. He helped lead OtherSide Entertainment along with the likes of fellow veteran developer Paul Neurath. The team released a stealth-action heist game called
Thick as Thieves
on May 30, which went through a massive reduction in scope. It was introduced as a larger competitive multiplayer immersive sim before being turned into a smaller, $5 game focused on single-player and co-op play.
OtherSide had another project in development, codenamed
Argos
, which was cancelled. This led to
17 jobs being cut
at the studio at the end of May. Weeks after, the team
laid off another group of employees
, making for a total of 36 people losing their jobs in just about a month.
The company, which received a
substantial investment
from Swedish game conglomerate Aonic in 2023, continued to employ "fewer than 10" people to performance maintenance on
Thick as Thieves
as of July, with no plans to work on any future games.
"To all of you reading this I want you to remember that games are not a solved problem yet—there is, I hope, plenty of experimentation and innovation to come," Spector's LinkedIn post says. "And to all you young developers out there, I've said it before and I'll say it again, your job is to make people forget people like me ever existed."
Related:
Triple-A vets and accessibility experts launch new game dev co-op: Raze and Rebuild Studio
He concludes: "Will I come back? Never say never. But I think it's time to ride off into the sunset. Now stop reading and make great games."
